question: The selling price of 50 books is equal to the cost price of 19 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given, 50 × SP = 19 × CP

⇒ SP / CP = 19 / 50

Here, CP = 50 units and SP = 19 units.

⇒ Loss = 50 − 19 = 31 units

⇒ Loss % = (31 / 50) × 100 = 62%

**∴ The correct answer is 62% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling price of 50 books = Cost price of 19 books

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 SP = 19 units
 Loss = 31 units
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total CP = 50 units
 Loss % = 31/50 × 100 = 62%

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of 1 book be ₹1.

⇒ CP of 50 books = ₹50

⇒ SP of 50 books = CP of 19 books = ₹19

Since CP > SP, a loss occurs.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP

⇒ Loss = 50 − 19 = ₹31

⇒ Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Loss % = (31 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 31 × 2 = 62%

**∴ The correct answer is 62% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formulas

Profit = SP − CP, and Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ False Weight) × 100

Marked Price & Discount

Discount = MP − SP, and Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100
